description: FR-PII-04. Korean writes the label before the value ('여권번호 M12345678'), so a confirming keyword within windowChars before a span is evidence about what the digits are. Each subtype declares what to do when that evidence is absent: keep it (the pattern stands on its own), or reject it (the shape alone is too common to report).

subtypes.basis: The pattern is one letter and eight digits, which is also the shape of model numbers, SKUs and ticket ids. Its 0.6 confidence was a hedge against exactly that. Every passport mention in Korean business writing carries the label, so requiring it removes the ambiguous half without costing a real detection.
A regional code plus grouped digits also describes equipment serial numbers and asset tags. Same trade as PASSPORT: the label is always present when the number really is a licence.

The checksum validator already rejects lookalikes such as an order number, so the pattern stands without a label. A label is still corroboration, so it raises confidence rather than deciding the detection.
An address is self-describing enough to report on its own, but a label distinguishes a customer's home address from a branch office named in passing.
